title: Arabian Nights: The Desert Crossing
project: a test project for the Immersive 2.0 direction-sheet instructions
brief: Arabian nights, a caravan crossing the desert at night, fully immersive: the listener is in the sand.
audience: a listener on a 7.1.2 system or headphones, no picture to follow, so the space has to carry the story
purpose: put the listener inside the crossing: the caravan passes, the room opens into a cistern at first light
point_of_view: the listener stands still on a dune and the caravan moves around them; nothing is ever in front for long
job: establish the desert at night as a place with no walls
make one pass-by audible as a pass-by, not a pan
let the room change at first light so the ending feels like arrival
put the listener in open air, so the first wall at the cistern is audible as a change
story: night falls on open sand, a caravan approaches from the left and crosses behind the listener, a mirage blooms and fades, and at first light the caravan reaches a stone cistern whose walls are the first walls in the piece.

sections.name: nightfall
sections.action: dusk over open sand, no landmark yet
sections.music: oud alone states the hijaz figure; the drone enters under it

sections.name: crossing
sections.action: a caravan appears far left and starts to cross
sections.music: ney takes the melody and travels; darbuka enters on maqsum; qanun answers

sections.name: mirage
sections.action: the air shimmers, a second caravan appears where there is none
sections.music: ululation over the full ensemble, qanun runs, ney overhead

sections.name: first_light
sections.action: the cistern wall appears; the caravan stops
sections.music: everything thins to oud and voice; the room becomes stone

motifs.name: the crossing figure
motifs.shape: D-Eb-F#-G, the half-flat second leaning up to the third
motifs.returns: every oud bar, and the ney sings it in augmentation at first light

motifs.name: the call
motifs.shape: a rising fourth answered a step lower
motifs.returns: behind the listener at the mirage, then in the cistern as a hum

avoid_sounds: any chant treated as a sample drop

hits.sound: the darbuka's first doum with the ney arriving overhead
hits.why: the crossing has to start somewhere a listener can point at

hits.sound: the ululation lands and the qanun run turns back down
hits.why: the mirage is the only moment of exultation before the arrival

must_hear: the ney crossing from left to behind at the mirage
the cistern's tail arriving before the last oud note ends

delivery.note: the engine renders at 44.1 kHz; stereo_48k is a target you add if a delivery needs 48 kHz

references: the sound of an oud recorded close in a dry room, a ney with breath left in it, a darbuka with no reverb on the dum
night desert ambience: no birds, wind low and wide, nothing above 6 kHz
gate_reason: an installation cue that builds and resolves, so the cinematic profile fits and its loudness target is the one the room expects

immersive.why: the caravan passes the listener from the left dune to behind them, and the room becomes stone at first light; both are the story, not decoration

movers.why: the caravan's approach is the cue's one long travel
movers.path: enters far left and low at the crossing, rises over the listener's head through the mirage, settles front-right at first light

movers.why: the mirage calls from behind, where a second caravan is not
movers.path: appears behind-left at the mirage, drifts to behind-right, leaves before the cistern

room_changes.what: open desert becomes a stone cistern: walls arrive, the tail grows and comes from the sides
room_changes.why: the first walls in the piece are the arrival

must_hear: the ney's pass from far left to behind, with its distance closing
the cistern's tail on the last oud note, arriving from the sides and above
the dune gust arriving from the left before the caravan does
immersive.notes: the sheet records intent; the presets execute it. Section names here are the vocabulary the ney's trajectory and the cistern scene are anchored to, and they match the score's plan.sections. Loudness is the two-channel master's number; the 7.1.2 and 7.1 files have their own -3.0 dBTP ceiling. The high voice is a sampled choir patch: the vocal engine's ululation left a measured click in the room return, so that part moved to a path that does not.

notes: No SFZ library for these instruments exists in the skill registry and sfizz cannot run on this Linux host, so every part plays the GM bank through presets; the SFZ block is left out rather than faked.
